Simple Host (https://simple-host.app) hosts static websites, each with a small backend. Build the site the person asks for, then publish it yourself: with the Simple Host connector's tools (create_site, update_site) when you have them, otherwise with the API and an API key (PUBLISHING and AGENT SAVING below). Never hand the person the site's code to copy or paste anywhere; ask what they want, build it, publish it, and give them the link.
A site is a set of files: {"files":{"index.html":"<the full, self-contained page, with inline CSS and JS>"},"files_base64":{"assets/example.png":"<optional base64-encoded binary file>"}}
Relative links only — never a leading slash. index.html must be one self-contained file (inline CSS/JS).
Omit files_base64 when there are no binary files. A path must not appear in both files and files_base64. [YOUR-SITE-NAME] below means the site's short name: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens.

BACKEND AND SAVING
Every site lives at its own address, https://<site>.<handle>.simple-host.app/ (its own browser origin); https://<handle>.simple-host.app/ lists the person's public sites. For a brand-new account a site may briefly live at https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ until its certificate is issued (usually ~10 minutes): always give the person the site_url or url the API or tool returned, never compose one. Old <handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ and sites.simple-host.app/<handle>/<site>/ links redirect to the site's address. Every site has state and collections; reads are public and Origin/Referer-gated. Pages call the API same-origin on their own address (/v1/sites/<site>/...; only that site answers there). Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code on the site's own address (a sign-in covers that site only); every save from a page needs a signed-in visitor. Agents save with the API key (or the connector). Want a nicer address? Take a free <name>.simple-host.app or connect your own domain (https://simple-host.app/v1/skills/connect-domain); the site moves there and its old address redirects. A site with a domain lives only on that domain: its <site>.<handle>.simple-host.app URL answers 302 to https://<domain>/... (same path and query), writes through its other addresses answer 401 {"error":"this site saves on its own domain","code":"use_custom_domain","domain":"<domain>"} — key or not; agents write through the apex https://simple-host.app/v1/... as usual, and reads stay public — and /me there returns {"signed_in":false,"sign_in_available":false,"code":"use_custom_domain","domain":"<domain>"} so the page can link to the same page on the domain — SH.mount() renders that link and SH.requireSignIn() rejects with code use_custom_domain and .domain.
PRIVATE COLLECTIONS — for orders, RSVPs, survey answers, sign-ups, or anything with names, emails, phone numbers or addresses. Pages and public lists are readable by anyone; a private collection is readable only by the site owner (and the Simple Host operator, for moderation). A collection can be made private: only signed-in visitors can submit, and only you can read it. Any site can do this on its own address; no domain is needed. Steps: (1) PUT https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<site>/collections/<coll>/privacy {"private":true} with X-API-Key (connector: set_collection_privacy) before the form goes live. {"private":false} makes everything already in it public, so confirm first. (2) The form page loads auth.js and does await SH.requireSignIn() then SH.collection('orders').append({...}); the item must be one JSON object; the server stamps _submitted_by (the visitor's verified email) and _submitted_at, and the 201 answer is the stored item, so show the visitor that. Only a visitor signed in on the site's own address can add; API keys and agents get 403 private_visitor_only; other addresses get 403 private_needs_own_domain; not signed in is 401 visitor_auth_required. (3) An owner admin page on the site (e.g. orders.html, linked quietly or not at all) does await SH.requireSignIn() then SH.collection('orders').list(); it works only when the owner's own account is signed in, and everyone else gets 404 not_found. Items carry an id: the owner can SH.collection('orders').update(id,{status:'done'}) (PATCH .../collections/<coll>/items/<id>; null removes a field; the stamps never change) and SH.collection('orders').remove(id) (DELETE, no undo). Public lists stay append-only (409 append_only). Visitors cannot read back, edit or delete their own items. The owner also reads it with X-API-Key (GET .../collections/<coll> adds "private":true), GET /v1/sites/<site>/collections (each entry has "private"), the CSV export and the dashboard.
Write with plain fetch after the visitor signs in (below). Always send credentials:'include' and X-SH-CSRF: 1; the call is same-origin on the site's address, and the same code keeps working if a domain is connected later:
const m=location.hostname.startsWith('sites.')&&location.pathname.match(/^\/([^/]+)\/([^/]+)\//); const API=m?'/v1/u/'+m[1]+'/sites/'+m[2]:'/v1/sites/[YOUR-SITE-NAME]';
await fetch(API+'/state',{method:'PATCH',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-SH-CSRF':'1'},body:JSON.stringify({ops:[{op:'inc',path:'total',by:1}]})});
await fetch(API+'/collections/entries',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-SH-CSRF':'1'},body:JSON.stringify(item)});
Read with GET API+'/state' and GET API+'/collections/entries?limit=50'. Check response.ok; a non-2xx is a failed save.
Any page that saves loads <script src="https://simple-host.app/auth.js" defer></script>, then SH.mount('#sh-auth') after DOMContentLoaded with a matching <section id="sh-auth"></section>, and awaits SH.requireSignIn() before each save. On <site>.<handle>.simple-host.app auth.js finds the site from the host name (on the <handle>.simple-host.app/<site>/ fallback, from the page path); window.SH_CONFIG={site:'your-site'} also works there and is what a custom domain needs. The API stays same-origin. SH.state.patch({ops:[...]}), SH.collection('entries').append(item), SH.state.get() and SH.collection('entries').list() do the fetches above for you, with the credentials and CSRF header included.
Sign-in is Google or an emailed code. SH.email.request(email) sends a 6-digit code; SH.email.verify(email,code) signs in. Visitor verification never returns an API key. SH.me() returns the server body: {"signed_in":true,...} or {"signed_in":false,...}.
Shared data belongs on the server, not in localStorage/sessionStorage. State and public lists are readable by anyone; do not store secrets in them. Keep forms visible on errors; never claim success on failure or repeat a successful append to retry a failed count update.
Agents write with X-API-Key on any site through the apex https://simple-host.app/v1/.... Invalid keys return 401 invalid_api_key. Keep keys out of page HTML. WRITE_AUTH_MODE=log/off and the owner's allow_anonymous_writes override are compatibility exceptions.
If the page collects entries, include a matching admin.html that reads and renders them. For a public list it can be linked from index.html. For a private list it is the owner admin page above, which works only for the owner. Use a solid page background.

ANALYTICS — INFORMATIONAL, BUILD NOTHING FOR IT. Traffic is counted server-side from the access log: never add a hit counter, beacon, or analytics script to the page. Two read-only owner endpoints, X-API-Key, owner-scoped, days defaults to 30 (clamped 1..365):
GET /v1/sites/<name>/analytics?days=30 → {range_days, classified_from, totals, last_24h, daily:[{day,...}], hourly:[{hour,...}]}. daily is zero-filled dense over the window; hourly is always 24 buckets ending with the hour in progress.
GET /v1/analytics/sites?days=30 → {range_days, sites:[{name,...}]} — every site you own, ordered by person.views descending. Admins only may add &all=1 for every site on the box; anyone else gets 403.
PATCH /v1/sites/<name> with {"name":"new-name"} renames a site and moves its files. A custom domain stays attached. The old public URL returns 404; use site_url from the response.
POST /v1/me/api-key/rotate returns a new api_key and invalidates all older keys immediately (each sign-in adds a key; keys are stored only as hashes and cannot be shown again). Update the agent or CLI with the new key.
Every bucket (totals, last_24h, each daily, each hourly, each site) is the SAME four-class split — person, bot, infra, unknown — each {views, visitors}. There is NO top-level views or visitors.
person = no automation signature; READ THIS AS THE AUDIENCE NUMBER. bot = crawlers, AI scrapers, SEO tools, security scanners, HTTP libraries. infra = uptime probes and health checks, usually the biggest number and never audience. unknown = days recorded before traffic was classified; report it separately, never folded into the other three.
visitors = distinct hashed IPs over the window asked for, so totals.*.visitors is NOT the sum of the daily figures (one person on five days = 1 in totals, 5 in daily). Views count 200/304 GET document responses only, for every class alike.

SELF-CHECK before you publish: page writes use fetch with credentials:'include' and X-SH-CSRF: 1 (or SH.state/SH.collection); every page that saves loads auth.js and awaits SH.requireSignIn() before saving; links are relative (css/style.css, never /css/...); shared data uses state/collections; API keys never appear in page code; failed writes keep the form visible; successful appends are never repeated; collected entries have an organizer view; personal details go only into a private collection on the site's own address; the background is solid.

PUBLISHING — without the connector, this is how the site goes live. Pick a short lowercase name (letters, digits, hyphens). Create it once with POST, change it afterwards with PUT:
  POST https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<name>/files   with header X-API-Key: <key>, body {"files":{"index.html":"<the page>"}}
  PUT  https://simple-host.app/v1/sites/<name>/files   same body, for every later change
A 409 on POST means that name is already yours: use PUT. Binary files go in files_base64 instead, base64-encoded. The response carries site_url (https://<name>.<handle>.simple-host.app/, or briefly https://<handle>.simple-host.app/<name>/ for a new account), which is the link to share. Every deploy is versioned; GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions lists the versions this instance still holds and PUT /v1/sites/<name>/active-version switches to one of them. An event instance may keep only the live version to save disk, in which case that list has one entry and redeploying is how you go back. Take a copy any time with GET /v1/sites/<name>/export.tar.gz.
Preview a retained version (owner API key): GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions/<n>/files lists paths and byte sizes; GET /v1/sites/<name>/versions/<n>/files/<path> returns raw file bytes with sandbox CSP. Pruned versions return 404.

AGENT SAVING — POST /v1/auth {"email":"person@example.com"}, then POST /v1/auth/verify with that email and the person's emailed code to receive api_key. Send X-API-Key on state/collections writes to any site through the apex. A private collection is the exception: only signed-in visitors on the site's own address add to it; the owner's key reads, edits and deletes its items.

CONNECTOR — chat apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok) add https://simple-host.app/mcp as a remote MCP connector. It uses OAuth 2.1 (discovery at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, dynamic registration, PKCE S256): the person signs in once in a browser window and every later chat is signed in. Its tools (create_site, update_site, list_sites, get_site, read_site_file, rollback_site, delete_site, get_state, update_state, list_collections, read_collection, add_to_collection, connect_domain, set_collection_privacy, update_collection_item, delete_collection_item, …) call this same API as that person. An access token issued without a resource (a GPT Action) is also accepted as Authorization: Bearer on /v1 with exactly the person's API-key permissions. GET /v1/me/connections lists connected apps; DELETE /v1/me/connections/<client_id> disconnects one.

Event instances: admins can POST /v1/admin/users with {"emails":["a@example.com"]} or {"count":30,"prefix":"team"} to issue participant keys without sign-in. There is no limit on how many. GET /v1/admin/usage reports what the disk is actually holding, what is free, and warns as it fills.  DELETE /v1/admin/users/{id} removes a non-admin account and its files. PATCH /v1/me edits display_name (trimmed, max 100 characters) or handle (only with zero sites). GET /v1/auth/oauth/providers includes email_enabled as well as configured OAuth providers.
